name: the Bois de Boulogne
title: Ancient Trees in the Bois de Boulogne, Paris: 6 to Find
meta_description: A 45 metre plane by the Serpentine, Bagatelle's 1840s planes and a cedar by the Grande Cascade, in the old royal forest Napoleon III remade as a park.
intro: By the city's register, a plane beside the Serpentine in the Bois de Boulogne stands 45 metres tall, close to the ceiling for its species anywhere. The stream it grows by is not natural. Alphand dug it under Napoleon III, when the old royal hunting forest was remade as a landscape park with two lakes and a waterfall of artificial rock, and most of the trees we map here arrived with that work or in the decades after it. The cedar of Lebanon beside the Grande Cascade was planted in 1862, the Serpentine plane and a giant sequoia in the Pré Catelan garden in 1872, and a Caucasian wingnut on the Lower Lake in 1882, close to the ferry for the Chalet des Iles. The oldest stand in Bagatelle, still a private estate when its planes went in between 1842 and 1847; one by the Orangerie reaches 40 metres. Bagatelle's sequoia carries a register date of 1850, three years before the species was first brought into cultivation in Britain, so that one date deserves some doubt. The woods are open and free, and Bagatelle charges a small fee from April to September.
